rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Microorganisms in household products ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Microorganisms in household products** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Microbes in Human Welfare fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  Fermentation is household chemistry. *Lactobacillus* turns milk into curd; yeast raises dough and ferments drinks; bacteria and fungi ripen cheese. Every one of these is a microbe digesting sugar and, as a by-product, changing the food — adding flavour, texture, preservation, and in the case of curd, nutrition (vitamin B12).

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Five products with microbes — curd (Lactobacillus, lactic acid), dough/idli-dosa (bacteria + yeast CO2), toddy (Saccharomyces), cheese (Propionibacterium holes; Roquefort fungi), bread (Saccharomyces cerevisiae).  ·  Trick 2: 'Roquefort cheese ripened by blue-green fungi; big holes in Swiss cheese from CO2 of Propionibacterium' — the two cheese specifics.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Summary.** Household fermentation is one principle in many costumes: the right microbe on a sugary food produces acid, alcohol or CO2 that textures, flavours and preserves the product. **Self-check:** can you match all seven products in the master table to their microbes?
